item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli police have detained ten settlers suspected of attacking a US photographer, a French mayor and other civilians in the West Bank, torching cars and olive trees and wounding farmers. The World Food Programme is ending food aid for half a million people in Gaza because of funding shortfalls. UNICEF reports that 340 children have been killed in Gaza despite a ceasefire. Israeli fire has killed five people in Gaza as private-sector goods are resumed into the enclave. The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
Turkish forces remain in Syria and Iraq until border security is assured, while Damascus officials warn Druze factions, allegedly backed by Israel, may launch attacks in Sweida. DNA-based identification of the missing offers families hope, and a security vacuum has seen 38 civilians killed in 33 homicides since early October. The Syrian court continues trials of three defendants in transitional justice cases, and regional partners discussed recovery and food security at Doha and FAO meetings. The UCDP recorded 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Ethiopian forces have installed a caretaker administration in Tigray and are moving toward the Eritrean border, while a pro-government militia says it has seized the regional airport and reports Eritrean forces suffered losses there. The United States, through Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is urging Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate the fighting. Mekelle mayor Shishay Amare announced elections will be held within six months and that Western Tigray will be settled through constitutional processes. Meanwhile, a drone strike in the disputed Abyei region killed at least 73 people, and the TPLF claims to have killed 1,511 Ethiopian soldiers in recent fighting. The conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:
Malian armed men stormed camps in the Menaka region, killing more than forty civilians in attacks attributed to Islamic State-linked militants. In Nigeria, gunmen attacked a convoy in Borno, killing fifteen soldiers and task force members, and terrorists killed soldiers at a Borno military post. Bandits raided two communities in Niger, causing scores of deaths. Mali’s military and allied armed groups continue to commit abuses against civilians. The conflict caused 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:
Gunmen in Plateau have killed an NSCDC officer and abducted a businessman, while separate attacks on herders in the same state left two dead and six injured. In Kaduna, bandits abducted five people including a one-month-old baby and a fisherman reported having his fingers cut off. Police freed a Catholic priest and seven others abducted in Benue, and bandits killed three policemen on duty in Zamfara. Islamist jihadists burned an evangelist alive in Adamawa and kidnapped a Catholic priest in Benue, also striking bases. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Afghan Taliban forces opened fire on Pakistani security forces along the Kurram border, prompting an intelligence-led army response that killed a Pakistani officer and several militants in Balochistan. Pakistan then suspended trade at two Iran border crossings, citing security and smuggling concerns, and trade with Afghanistan fell sharply after border closures. The government announced plans to open a consulate in Benghazi, Libya, while the navy outlined a new strategy pairing mesh networking with long-range strike capability. Protesters burned effigies of the chief minister and deputy chief minister and placed bodies of killed civilians outside the chief minister’s residence, demanding resignations. In Kashmir, the Northern Army commander reviewed security and operational preparedness while buses bound for the region were attacked in Punjab and Haryana, with passengers labeled terrorists. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Philippines: the situation
item.description:
Chinese officials summoned China’s ambassador after his warning of using force, while Philippine lawmakers demanded an apology and a review of water-cannon rules. Vice Admiral Rommel Supangan assumed command of the Philippine Coast Coast Guard and led a rescue of four people, including a child, on Hagonoy Island, Surigao del Sur. Chinese coast guard and navy vessels entered waters near the Pratas Islands and Scarborough Shoal, and Taiwan’s coast guard and maritime forces repelled sixteen mainland Chinese ships in a coordinated operation. The United States and the Philippines conducted their sixteenth bilateral maritime exercise in the West Philippine Sea, and there were 176 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Southern Thailand: the situation
item.description:
Violent attacks persisted in the insurgency zone, with pipe bombs wounding army officers and security volunteers in Narathiwat and Yala and grenade attacks in Trang leading to arrests and seizure of explosives. A Chinese suspect was detained in Bangkok after attempting a 100,000 baht border crossing, and Malaysia appointed a new facilitator for southern Thailand peace talks. Cambodia and Thailand agreed on confidence-building measures at a UNCLOS meeting and discussed easing maritime border tensions, while the WTO and multilateral partners reviewed progress on a supply-chain finance initiative. Floods in Thailand killed 80 people as waters receded, and there were 35 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Ukrainian-origin fiber-optic drones are being trained for use by Mexican cartels, prompting continued border patrol challenges from drone incursions. European and Ecuadorian police cooperation produced 20 arrests in a major drug-trafficking bust, and nightly curfews were imposed across Ecuador from November 1 to 10 under a state of emergency. item.description:

Iran-backed Iraqi militias have pledged to defend Iran if attacked, while Iraqi authorities are pursuing legal action against media incitement supporting pro-Iran armed groups and have arrested a lawyer who brandished a gun in court. The Shingal mayoral post, vacant for nine years, is now open for nominations, and Jordan's king reaffirmed support for regional sovereignty and security. In Ruweng, fresh attacks left nine dead and six wounded, while in Northern Bahr el Ghazal bodies arrived from Khor Kaltan killings. item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Fitgharan forces now hold the Mogadishu-Baidoa corridor while Laftagareen forces have seized Buurhakaba and another town in the Bay region, expanding fighting in southern Somalia. Al Shabaab detonated an IED in Mandera, injuring six civilians, and the ICRC treated 148 wounded after heavy combat in Baidoa. Ethiopia announced the withdrawal of more than 3,000 troops from Somalia as its own civil war intensifies, and Ethiopia has refused to intervene in the South West State conflict. Somaliland and Puntland were designated as "friendly" in an Israeli security framework, and Somalia is screening travelers after Kenya confirmed an imported Ebola case and has agreed to acquire Pakistani JF‑17 fighter jets. The UCDP recorded 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Recent attacks have also hit a market in southern Sudan and an artisanal gold mine in South Kordofan, killing children and many civilians. These strikes expand the use of drones from combatant targets to economic and civilian locations, increasing civilian casualties.
